whyItExists.problem: Programs need to make decisions — show this if logged in, show that otherwise. Without conditionals, every program runs the same code path regardless of input.
whyItExists.solution: Conditional statements execute different blocks of code based on whether conditions are true or false. JavaScript provides if/else, switch, and the ternary operator.
whyItExists.whenToUse: Any time a program must choose between two or more code paths based on a value or condition.
whyItExists.whenNotToUse: For repeated actions, use loops. For complex decision trees, consider a lookup object or map instead of long if/else chains.

explainModes.beginner: A conditional is a 'yes or no' question your code asks. 'Is the user logged in? Yes → show dashboard. No → show login page.' You write this with if (condition) { ... } else { ... }.
explainModes.simple: if checks a condition and runs a block if true. else if adds more conditions. else is the fallback. The ternary operator is a shorthand for simple if/else. switch compares one value against many cases.
explainModes.standard: JavaScript evaluates conditions as truthy/falsy. Falsy values: false, 0, '', null, undefined, NaN. Everything else is truthy. switch uses strict equality (===) for case matching. break prevents fall-through to the next case.
explainModes.technical: The ternary operator is an expression — it returns a value and can be used inside other expressions. switch fall-through is intentional when multiple cases share a handler. The optional chaining (?.) and nullish coalescing (??) operators often replace simple conditionals for null checks.
explainModes.deepDive: Conditional branches affect JavaScript engine optimisation. V8's Turbofan inline-cache misses occur when a conditional switches between returning different object shapes — the engine assumes the hot path stays consistent. Prefer early returns to deeply nested if/else trees for both readability and predictable type profiles.

questions.question: Which of these values is TRUTHY in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: An empty array [] is truthy in JavaScript. 0, empty string '', and null are all falsy. This surprises many beginners — always use explicit checks like array.length === 0 to test for empty arrays.

questions.question: What does 'fall-through' mean in a switch statement?
options: The switch falls back to if/else
Without break, execution continues into the next case
questions.explanation: Without a break statement, a matched case 'falls through' and continues executing the next case's code. This can be intentional (multiple cases sharing code) or a bug.

faq.q: When should I use switch instead of if/else if?
faq.a: switch is cleaner when you are comparing one variable against many discrete values (day names, status codes). if/else is better when conditions involve ranges, multiple variables, or complex logic.

faq.q: What is an early return and why is it useful?
faq.a: Returning early from a function when a condition is not met avoids deeply nested if/else. Instead of if (valid) { ... lots of code ... }, write if (!valid) return; and continue with the happy path at the same indentation level.

A dark/light mode toggle uses a ternary: theme = theme === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark'
